# Cadence

> Cadence is a gym habit app for iPhone that notices when you arrive at your gym and counts the visit automatically. No workout logging.

Cadence is for people whose problem is turning up, not what to lift. You set a weekly target (for example, three times a week), the days you mean to go and your gym. After that there is nothing to do: the phone's geofencing notices when you arrive, and a stay of 20 minutes or more counts as a visit, even with the app closed.

Key facts:

- App Store name: Cadence: Gym Habit (iPhone). Coming soon to the App Store.
- Category: gym habit app. Not a workout logger: no sets, reps, weights or calories.
- How it counts: automatic gym check-in by geofence. 20-minute minimum stay.
- Progress: a weekly ring (visits against target) and a streak counted in weeks, with one missed week a month forgiven automatically.
- Reminders: short notifications on planned days, written never to guilt or shame. A missed session gets "All good — tomorrow's there if you want it."
- Privacy: only the gym's location is stored, never a trail of where you have been. Visits are stored as start and end times without coordinates. No advertising or analytics software.
- Price: free, always, for counting visits, history, streak and account. Cadence Plus (£2.99 a month, £17.99 a year or £39.99 once) adds more than one gym and four extra voices for the reminders.
- Made by an independent developer in the UK.
- Works well alongside a workout logger such as Strong or Hevy: Cadence gets you there, the logger tracks what you do.
